answer: When a handle changes, the owner publishes a signed record linking the old handle to the new one, preserving a verifiable history. An attacker cannot claim someone else old handle because the link needs the owner signature, and a Sybil operator cannot erase the history that ties its fake accounts to their past names. A kernel that appears twice is the tell: the same proof cannot recover twice. When the river settles over the haven, the account stands because every recovery carried its own proof.
